accepted.s: The Bengal Sati Regulation of 1829 was issued as which Regulation of the Bengal Code?
accepted.x: The Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829, was Regulation XVII of the Bengal Code. It declared Sati illegal and punishable.
accepted.tq: Use the exact-number trap by distinguishing the regulation number from nearby legal provisions.
accepted.sec: Abolition of Sati - Governor-General, regulation, role of reformers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Bengal Sati Regulation declaring Sati illegal was dated:
accepted.x: Lord William Bentinck issued the Bengal Sati Regulation on 4 December 1829.
accepted.tq: Fix the event by separating the date of the Bengal regulation from the later extension to other Presidencies.
accepted.sec: Abolition of Sati - Governor-General, regulation, role of reformers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With regard to the territorial application of the Bengal Sati Regulation, which one of the following is correct?
o: It was extended to Madras and Bombay Presidencies in 1828.
It was extended to Punjab and Sindh in 1830.
It was extended to Madras and Bombay Presidencies in 1830.
It was extended only to Bombay Presidency in 1831.
accepted.x: The regulation was extended to the Madras and Bombay Presidencies in 1830.
accepted.tq: Test the location-and-year pair, a common APPSC trap involving expansion of a law.
accepted.sec: Abolition of Sati - Governor-General, regulation, role of reformers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the abolition of Sati:
1. Rammohan Roy conducted a long campaign against the practice.
2. Raja Radhakant Deb supported the Sati ban through the Dharma Sabha.
3. The Dharma Sabha was founded in 1830.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Raja Radhakant Deb founded the orthodox Dharma Sabha in opposition to the Brahmo propaganda and the Sati ban, so statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped stance: the orthodox organisation opposed, rather than supported, the reform.
accepted.sec: Abolition of Sati - Governor-General, regulation, role of reformers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the principal objective of the Atmiya Sabha associated with Rammohan Roy?
o: Translation of the Upanishads and Vedanta into Bengali and English
Promotion of military education among Indians
Campaign for the exclusive use of Sanskrit in education
Organisation of peasant resistance in Bengal
accepted.x: The Atmiya Sabha, or Society of Friends, was associated with translating the Upanishads and Vedanta into Bengali and English.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution from its distinctive activity rather than from its founder alone.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj - founding year, original name, founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Brahmo Sabha founded in Calcutta in 1828 was established by Rammohan Roy in association with:
accepted.x: Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in association with Dwarkanath Tagore in Calcutta in 1828.
accepted.tq: Use the founder-associate distinction to avoid confusing different Tagores connected with the movement.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj - founding year, original name, founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The institution originally known as the Brahmo Sabha came to be known as the Brahmo Samaj after it was renamed by:
accepted.x: The Brahmo Sabha was later renamed the Brahmo Samaj by Maharishi Debendranath Tagore.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the founder of an organisation and the later person associated with its renaming.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj - founding year, original name, founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Organisation)
a. Brahmo Samaj of India
b. Sadharan Brahmo Samaj
c. Prarthana Samaj
 d. Paramahansa Mandali

List-II (Year)
i. 1849
ii. 1866
iii. 1867
iv. 1878
accepted.x: The Brahmo Samaj of India was formed in 1866, the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj in 1878, the Prarthana Samaj in 1867 and the Paramahansa Mandali in 1849.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure year-pair and eliminate codes containing a conflicting chronological association.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj - founding year, original name, founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Organisation)
a. Sadharan Brahmo Samaj
b. Seva Sadan
c. Deva Samaj
d. Dharma Sabha

List-II (Founder)
i. Behramji Malabari
ii. Shiv Narayan Agnihotri
iii. Anandamohan Bose and Sivanath Sastri
iv. Radhakant Deb
accepted.x: The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj was founded by Anandamohan Bose and Sivanath Sastri; Seva Sadan by Behramji Malabari; Deva Samaj by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri; and Dharma Sabha by Radhakant Deb.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure founder-organisation pair and check that no founder is repeated in the code.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj - founding year, original name, founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Dharma Sabha was founded by Raja Radhakant Deb, not Keshab Chandra Sen. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong founder-organisation pair by applying the swapped-person trap.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj - founding year, original name, founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following organisations was founded in Poona in 1849 to oppose caste distinctions and promote women’s education?
accepted.x: Paramahansa Mandali was founded by Dadoba Pandurang in 1849 and was associated with opposition to caste distinctions and support for women’s education.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation by combining its place, year and reform objective.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj - founding year, original name, founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Raja Rammohan Roy:
1. He lived from 1772 to 1833.
2. He knew Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit and English.
3. He died at Bristol.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Rammohan Roy lived from 1772 to 1833, knew the four languages mentioned and died at Bristol in 1833.
accepted.tq: Confirm each biographical statement independently before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Rammohan Roy - titles, 'Raja', visit to England  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Raja Rammohan Roy’s journey to England is generally placed in which year in the commonly used account?
accepted.x: Rammohan Roy left for England in 1830; some accounts associate the mission and title with 1831, but the commonly cited departure year is 1830.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the departure year from the year of his death and from the closely associated 1831 reference.
accepted.sec: Rammohan Roy - titles, 'Raja', visit to England  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the title and mission associated with Rammohan Roy?
o: Akbar II conferred the title ‘Raja’ and sent him to England as his envoy.
William Bentinck conferred the title ‘Raja’ and sent him to England as his envoy.
Keshab Chandra Sen conferred the title ‘Raja’ and sent him to England as his envoy.
Debendranath Tagore conferred the title ‘Raja’ and sent him to England as his envoy.
accepted.x: Mughal emperor Akbar II conferred the title ‘Raja’ on Rammohan Roy and sent him to England as his envoy.
accepted.tq: Ask who would perform the act, using the authority-and-person trap.
accepted.sec: Rammohan Roy - titles, 'Raja', visit to England  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin is correct?
o: It was an English work defending idolatry.
It was a Persian work written against idolatry.
It was a Bengali journal dealing with social reform.
It was a Sanskrit work on the rituals of the Brahmo Samaj.
accepted.x: Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin, meaning A Gift to Monotheists, was a Persian book of Rammohan Roy written against idolatry.
accepted.tq: Combine the work’s exact title, language and theme to defeat look-alike book options.
accepted.sec: Rammohan Roy - books and journals → language  [other exams]

accepted.s: Rammohan Roy’s work titled Precepts of Jesus — the Guide to Peace and Happiness was written in:
accepted.x: Precepts of Jesus — the Guide to Peace and Happiness was written in English and presented a rational ethical interpretation of Jesus’s teachings.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among the languages associated with Rammohan Roy’s different books and journals.
accepted.sec: Rammohan Roy - books and journals → language  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Debendranath Tagore — Tattvabodhini Sabha and Tattvabodhini Patrika
Keshab Chandra Sen — Dharma Sabha and Tattvabodhini Patrika
Radhakant Deb — Tattvabodhini Sabha and Brahmo Samaj of India
Dwarkanath Tagore — Deva Samaj and Tattvabodhini Patrika
accepted.x: Debendranath Tagore founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839, whose Bengali organ was the Tattvabodhini Patrika.
accepted.tq: Match the reformer with both the organisation and its publication rather than with a rival institution.
accepted.sec: Debendranath Tagore - Tattvabodhini Sabha and Patrika  [other exams]

accepted.s: The main purpose of the Tattvabodhini Patrika was to:
o: Defend orthodox opposition to the abolition of Sati
Publish official regulations of the Bengal Government
Spread Rammohan Roy’s ideas through a Bengali organ
Promote the use of Persian as the language of administration
accepted.x: The Bengali Tattvabodhini Patrika spread the ideas of Rammohan Roy through the efforts of the Tattvabodhini Sabha.
accepted.tq: Infer the function of a reform journal from its associated organisation and language.
accepted.sec: Debendranath Tagore - Tattvabodhini Sabha and Patrika  [other exams]

accepted.s: Debendranath Tagore revived the Brahmo Samaj after Rammohan Roy’s death by stressing:
o: The restoration of Sati as a religious duty
Rejection of idolatry and rituals and worship of the formless God
accepted.x: Debendranath Tagore stressed rejection of idolatry and rituals and advocated worship of the formless God while reviving the Brahmo Samaj.
accepted.tq: Select the option that preserves the reform movement’s defining religious principle and reject the reversed alternatives.
accepted.sec: Debendranath Tagore - Tattvabodhini Sabha and Patrika  [other exams]

accepted.s: The title ‘Maharishi’ is associated with:
accepted.x: Debendranath Tagore was known by the title ‘Maharishi’.
accepted.tq: Use the title-person association while distinguishing it from Rammohan Roy’s title ‘Raja’.
accepted.sec: Debendranath Tagore - Tattvabodhini Sabha and Patrika  [other exams]
